action: 1984 customers: watch the company's own channels for restoration; the company says email and DNS come back first, then other services once it is satisfied that customer data and systems are secure.
date_note: 1984's statement was published on 20 November, the day the shutdown began.
exec: An Icelandic hosting provider took its services offline after an attack it calls well-planned and technically advanced, and says it cannot yet say when all services will be normal.
geo_basis: country (company location not stated in the source)
plain: Icelandic web host 1984 shut down its services on 20 November after what it calls a well-planned and technically advanced attack. Xakep.ru reports it later said attackers stole part of its internal data.

sources.name: DV: joint statement of 1984 ehf. and CERT-IS, 20 Nov 2026

summary: Icelandic web host 1984 shut down its services on 20 November after a cyberattack; in its statement the company says initial findings suggest a well-planned and technically advanced attack, and that it cannot yet say when all services will be normal. Xakep.ru reports that 1984 later said attackers stole part of its internal data, and that CERT-IS's head said the attackers clearly used AI. Responsibility has not been stated.
title: Icelandic web host 1984 takes services offline after major cyberattack, managing director says

validation.note: 1984 ehf. and CERT-IS joint statement (DV, 20 Nov) is primary; Iceland Review (21 Nov, relaying RUV) and Xakep.ru (23 Nov) also read. Xakep's claims of AI use and data theft come from Xakep only (it relays Icelandic media pages that did not load for me).
